title: Ferries, Trains & Emergencies
whatItIs: On a ferry or train, a regular daily rest can be interrupted twice, for no more than 1 hour in total. In exceptional circumstances you can depart from the rules to reach a safe stopping place.
keyFacts: Ferry or train: a regular daily rest can be interrupted twice, 1 hour in total.
You need a sleeper cabin, bunk or couchette, and the rest must still total 11 hours (12 if split).
A regular weekly rest: only on a crossing of 8 hours or more, with a sleeper cabin.

keyFacts.text: On a digital tachograph you MUST select ferry mode as well as rest mode when using this rule.

keyFacts: Unforeseen events (e.g. severe weather): you may depart from the rules to reach a safe stop.

keyFacts.text: You MUST note the reasons on a printout or chart, at the latest when you reach the stopping place.

visual.caption: When the drivers' hours rules can bend

items.title: Ferry or train
items.text: Interrupt a regular daily rest twice at most, 1 hour in total.

items.title: Unforeseen event
items.text: Only as far as needed to reach a suitable stopping place.

items.title: Reaching base or home
items.text: Up to 1 hour extra, or 2 hours after a 30-minute break.

items.title: Emergency
items.text: Vehicles in emergency or rescue operations are exempt.

a.label: Unforeseen event
points: Unexpected delay: e.g. severe weather, collision, breakdown

b.label: Emergency
points: Immediate action needed, e.g. to avoid danger to life or health
Vehicles in emergency or rescue operations are exempt

onTheTest.question: You take a regular daily rest on an overnight ferry. What is the most total interruption allowed?
onTheTest.why: No more than twice, and 1 hour in total, to drive on and off and for customs.

onTheTest.question: Heavy snow delays you and you will go over your driving time. What may you do?
options: Only go on to a suitable stopping place
Ignore the rules for the day
Ask your employer to edit the record
onTheTest.why: You may depart from the rules only as far as needed to reach a suitable stopping place, if road safety is not put at risk.

traps: Planned breaches are never unforeseen: the rules only bend for genuine, unexpected delays.
Extra driving must be paid back: equivalent rest in one block by the end of the third week after.
You still need your 11-hour (or 9-hour) daily rest, even if it can't be finished within 24 hours.
